vo_text: Cities run hotter than the land around them, and the hottest blocks are the most paved, the least green, the most lived-in. A Barcelona heat officer has one budget, and one question: where do you plant the trees?

captions.text: Cities run hotter than the countryside
Hottest blocks: most paved, least green
One budget. Where do we plant?

vo_text: CoolSpend answers it. It maps the hot, paved, unshaded ground, then greedily places each tree where its real shadow actually falls, south of the heat. Diminishing returns give it a guarantee: within sixty-three percent of the perfect answer, every euro spent where it cools the most.

captions.text: Map the hot, paved, unshaded ground
Place trees where the shadow falls

vo_text: Then it stops proposing and starts measuring. The chosen layout is re-simulated on the live Infrared UTCI engine. On one plaza: twenty trees cool two thousand seven hundred and seventy-nine square metres of ground by at least half a degree, at seventy-two euros a square metre. Measured, not estimated.

Scale it to the city. Give it a million euros, and it ranks all four hundred ninety-four blocks and funds the hottest first. Ninety trees across six districts, twenty thousand square metres cooled, reaching about twenty-six thousand residents within a three-hundred-metre walk.
And every number is honest. Three backends, mock, cached, and live, keep a synthetic preview from ever masquerading as a measurement. The rule is simple: never report a number we did not compute.

captions.text: No synthetic preview posing as measured
Never report a number we didn't compute

vo_text: Real geometry, real ecology, real budgets. A plan a city can defend. CoolSpend. Fidelity, not novelty.

captions.text: A plan a city can defend
